solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gem set tight in a hollow

indicators.note: tight means drunk, and a drunken word staggers out of its proper order
the jumbled word is placed in the middle of the following pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then jumbled
a ria is a long narrow inlet formed by a drowned river valley

explanation.surface: A jeweller fixes a stone firmly into a recess cut for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set tight' reads as a jeweller's instruction, but tight (drunk) is what scrambles 'set'. A + RIA hold the result: A-STE-RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteria is an old name for a star stone, a gem showing a star-shaped gleam when cut, such as star sapphire.

clue.text: Those trying to stay on the wagon about to turn over wagon?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps itself round the other

blocks.clueFragment: Those trying to stay on the wagon
blocks.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members try to stay off drink
to turn over a house is slang for burgling it

explanation.surface: Recovering drinkers wonder whether to tip over a wagon, a joke on 'on the wagon'.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'wagon' belongs to the idiom for staying sober; only the final one is the definition, and its question mark admits the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroba (or araba) is a heavy covered cart used in Turkey and India, so it is a kind of wagon.

clue.text: Backing a small local branch to stock right range

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read from the end
to stock something is to hold it inside, as a shop holds goods

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
reis is a dialect word for twigs, small branches or brushwood

explanation.surface: Supporting a small local bank branch that holds stock for the right range of customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word, as Mephisto clues often do; 'branch' and 'stock' pretend to be about banking or shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a range of mountains with jagged peaks, especially in Spain or the Americas.

clue.text: Not good to knock state of France

indicators.note: 'not good' asks for the abbreviation for good to be left out of the next word

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to get at someone is to criticise or knock them

explanation.surface: Criticising France is not a good idea.
explanation.walkthrough: GET AT loses its G to leave the French word for state.
explanation.definitionFit: Etat is the French noun for a state or nation, as in coup d'etat.

clue.text: In river spot almost root-like structure

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
'in river' says the next piece sits inside the name of a river

blocks.note: the Rhine, the great European river
a zit is a pimple or spot

explanation.surface: A spot in a river almost looks like a root.
explanation.walkthrough: ZI(T) goes into RHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhizine is a root-like strand by which a lichen or moss is attached to the surface it grows on.

clue.text: Use part of friary as a major religious school

indicators.note: taking only part of a run of words means the answer is sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone proposes turning part of a friary into a big religious school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded in 1875, a school of religious thought rather than a building.

clue.text: Collar about the same as veil?

indicators.note: about means round the outside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to collar a criminal is to nab or arrest them
i.q. abbreviates Latin idem quod, the same as

explanation.surface: Asks whether a collar is much the same thing as a veil.
explanation.walkthrough: IQ here is not intelligence but the Latin abbreviation idem quod, found in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A niqab is the face veil worn by some Muslim women, leaving the eyes uncovered.

clue.text: How I may be described is receiving a lot of stink

indicators.note: a lot of the word, but not all of it, so its final letter goes
receiving means taking in, so the short word wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a stink is a bad odour

explanation.surface: Someone describing themself is taking in a strong smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital I is the chemical symbol for iodine, not the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodous means containing iodine, in the lower valency, so it describes the element whose symbol is I.

clue.text: Plants will grow back after deadheading and cutting leaves

indicators.note: deadheading a flower removes its head, so the first letter is cut off
back says the shortened word is to be read the other way round
cutting into a word means breaking it open and lodging inside it

blocks.note: 'll is the contraction of will, as in I'll
taken as written
quits as a verb, departs or leaves

explanation.surface: A gardener promises that plants will regrow once spent flowers and cuttings are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage, which suits the gardening picture, but it is the verb for departs. 'Will' is cut to its contracted form, as in I'll.
explanation.definitionFit: Quillworts are small aquatic plants related to clubmosses, with stiff quill-like leaves.

clue.text: Leaves for Thatchers aiming to taste apple products primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the initials of five words

explanation.surface: Thatchers, the cider maker, wants people to try its apple products.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatchers is a West Country cider brand, which suits 'apple products'; here the word just means people who thatch roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Attap is the palm thatch of Malaysia, the leaves of the nipa palm used for roofing huts.

clue.text: What'll give a buzz after exercising right away, Bovril? (7, two words)

indicators.note: right away means the abbreviation for right is taken out
exercising works the letters about, moving them into new positions

blocks.note: a bee buzzes
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Asks whether a cup of Bovril gives you a lift straight after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word but is the fodder: lose its R, rearrange AFTE, and put BEE in front. Bovril is a British beef extract made into a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a drink made from beef extract, and Bovril is the best-known brand of it.

clue.text: Scottish Wanderer at home hit three in drubbing

indicators.note: a word that has been hit is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
in says the pieces before it go inside the following word

blocks.note: at home is in
taken as written, then rearranged
a drubbing is a heavy defeat, a rout

explanation.surface: A Scottish team called Wanderers scores three at home in a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanderer' looks like a football club's name, but it is a vagrant; 'hit' looks like scoring but is only shaking up 'three'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rin-there-out is a Scots word for a vagabond, literally someone who runs there and out.

clue.text: Performed awful dirge on old instrument

indicators.note: an awful version of a word is a mangled one with its letters in a bad order

blocks.note: did, as in did a turn on stage
taken as written, then rearranged
o' is a shortened form of on, as in o' nights
O is an abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone played a dreadful funeral song on an antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is the long wooden drone pipe of Aboriginal Australia, a wind instrument.

clue.text: Explosive end to barbecue after drunk returns having left earlier

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word is read from its end
the abbreviation for left is brought forward one place to come earlier in the word
the end of a word is its final letter
after says the barbecue piece is placed second, behind the piece for drunk

blocks.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
the final letter of barbecue

explanation.surface: The drunk came back and left early, and the barbecue ended explosively.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiddly is mild British slang for tipsy. 'Left' looks like a verb for the drunk departing, but it is the abbreviation L, moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyddite is a high explosive made from picric acid, named after Lydd in Kent where it was tested.

clue.text: Bask extravagantly around luxury carriages

indicators.note: extravagantly suggests wild excess, letters thrown about out of order
around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the Ritz is the London hotel that stands for luxury, as in ritzy

explanation.surface: An invitation to lounge lavishly among luxuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bask' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is the fodder; the Ritz is the London hotel whose name means luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: A britzka is an open horse-drawn carriage from Poland with a folding hood, and room to lie down.

clue.text: Cute Aussie being left in karaoke bar knocking out Wings hit

indicators.note: in says one piece is put inside the other
knocking out the wings removes the two outermost letters and keeps the middle
the letters are struck about and land in a new order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
both end letters removed

explanation.surface: A karaoke bar singer, minus their friend who left, belts out a hit by Paul McCartney's band Wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings hit' looks like a song title by McCartney's band; in fact the Wings are the outer letters of 'karaoke bar' and hit is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A koala bear is the cuddly-looking Australian marsupial, so a cute being from down under.

clue.text: A king running even parts of Kildare?

definitions.text: A king running even parts of Kildare?

indicators.note: the even parts of a word are its second, fourth and sixth letters
running letters move about and finish in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is for rex, king
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A king who ruled over parts of County Kildare in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the Ard Ri was a king, and even an Irish High King ruled lands like Kildare.
explanation.definitionFit: Ard ri is Irish for high king, the overlord of the kings of Ireland's provinces.

clue.text: Old school with covering of persistent mould

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

blocks.note: scul is an obsolete spelling of school, as in a shoal of fish
the outermost letters

explanation.surface: An old school building is coated in mould that will not go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like a fungus noun to go with the damp old school; it is the verb to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To sculpt is to shape a material into form, which is what to mould means as a verb.

clue.text: Finish off beer and knock back a new bottle

indicators.note: finishing off a word here means cutting off its last letter
back says the following short piece is read in the other direction

blocks.note: lager is a beer
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Down your beer and sink another fresh bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' wants to mean drink, which suits the beer; here it only turns the next letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagena is an ancient narrow-necked flask, a type of bottle.

clue.text: Hamilton's shy, it's not all his fault sadly

indicators.note: not all of the words are used, so one letter is left behind
sadly suggests things going wrong, the letters falling into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, less one S

explanation.surface: Someone named Hamilton is timid, though not entirely through his own fault.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamilton is a town near Glasgow, so 'Hamilton's shy' means the Scots word for shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laithfu is Scots for bashful, literally loathful, as used in a Scottish town such as Hamilton.

clue.text: What punters fix to start to rake in huge amounts

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of two words
a peck is a large amount, as in a peck of trouble

explanation.surface: Gamblers fixing races to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punters' looks like gamblers; they are people propelling punts on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripeck (or rypeck) is a pole stuck into a riverbed to moor a punt, so something punters fix in place.

clue.text: Close to Tories getting small swing in Scotland

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: the final letter
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Election talk: the Conservatives see a small swing towards them in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing' reads as an electoral shift; it is the verb or noun for swaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Swee is a Scots word for a swing or sway, also a verb for swinging back and forth.

clue.text: Birds section moved to back of store

indicators.note: s. abbreviates section, and that letter is shifted from the front round to the far end

blocks.note: to store something is to save it

explanation.surface: The bird department of a shop has been relocated to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' and 'store' look like a shop's layout; section only names the letter that moves, by its abbreviation s.
explanation.definitionFit: Aves is the scientific name of the class of birds in zoology.

clue.text: Wrong to provide conclusion for Turin shroud

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
to do food is to provide it, as in 'they do lunches'
the last letter

explanation.surface: It would be wrong to settle the question of the Turin Shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turin Shroud is the linen cloth some believe wrapped Christ's body; only 'shroud' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sindon is a fine linen cloth, especially a burial shroud; the Turin relic is often called the Holy Sindone.

clue.text: Buck's Fizz largely lip-sync Heart of Stone with oomph

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter is lost
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: to mime is to lip-sync
the central letter of the five
SA, sex appeal, is oomph

explanation.surface: Bucks Fizz, the pop group, mostly mime to a song called Heart of Stone, with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks Fizz were the British pop group who won Eurovision in 1981 and did record 'Heart of Stone', so the surface reads as music news.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimosa is a cocktail of orange juice and champagne, the American name for a Buck's Fizz.

clue.text: Prime time star's making a comeback leaving Britain

indicators.note: a comeback returns from the far end, so the pieces are read backwards
leaving here means departing from, so the abbreviation for Britain is taken out

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a star is a celeb, with the 's
B is the abbreviation for Britain

explanation.surface: A star's prime-time comeback show involves leaving Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: T + CELEBS turned round gives SBELECT; taking out B leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime and select are both adjectives for the best or choicest, as in prime or select cuts.

clue.text: Italy international capturing knight with rook by acting on impulse

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the two single letters enclose others

blocks.note: I is the international car code for Italy
N is the chess notation for knight
R is the chess notation for rook
I is an abbreviation for international
x is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in two by four
a. is the abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

explanation.surface: An Italian international footballer is booked for a rash challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: I + I capture N and R, the chess knight and rook, then X and A follow. 'Acting on impulse' looks like one phrase, but acting supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In rixa is Latin for in a quarrel, used of words or acts done in the heat of the moment without forethought.

clue.text: Old 'un's aggrieved once refused

indicators.note: aggrieved suggests upset, so the letters are disturbed into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The old fellow is upset at having been turned down in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nould is Spenser's contraction of ne would, meaning would not, an archaic way to say refused.

clue.text: Piles brought back some misery perhaps

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of them is used, a run of letters inside
brought back means returned, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Haemorrhoids have brought back some of the old misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' wants to be the medical complaint, which fits the misery; it means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyres are piles of wood built for burning, especially funeral pyres.

clue.text: Chauffeur given tip for excursion, silver money

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its leading point, its first letter

blocks.note: a syce is a groom in India, and later a driver
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A chauffeur receives a tip for taking passengers on an outing, in silver coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, which suits the chauffeur; it marks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycee is fine silver cast in ingots, formerly used as currency in China.

clue.text: Woefully caught in stream inside well

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second
inside places the combined piece within the final word

blocks.note: doing something well is doing it ably
a jet is a stream of liquid
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is miserably trapped down a well with water running into it.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into JET, and JECT goes into ABLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Abjectly means wretchedly or miserably, just as woefully means in a pitiful way.

clue.text: It's hard to get nicked by better shaver

indicators.note: to be nicked by a word means to be grabbed and held inside it

blocks.note: to cap is to better or outdo
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A better razor makes it harder to cut yourself shaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaver' looks like a razor, which suits 'nicked'; a young shaver is a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaver is an informal word for a boy or fellow, as is chap.

clue.text: Secret meetings? Don't get caught in embraces with husband

indicators.note: not getting something means it is missing, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
cuddles are embraces

explanation.surface: Lovers meeting in secret are warned not to be caught cuddling with a husband about.
explanation.walkthrough: H joins (C)UDDLES. The question mark admits that huddles are only secret in that they are private conferences.
explanation.definitionFit: A huddle is a private conference, as when a team huddles to plan in secret.

clue.text: Disapprovingly watch ladies perhaps serve out-of-date mouldy cakes round back of canteen

indicators.note: mouldy means gone off and decayed, so the letters break down into another order
the back of a word is its final letter
round says the rearranged letters go all the way round the next piece

blocks.note: the ladies is a public toilet, a loo
ka is an obsolete word for serve, as in 'ka me, ka thee'
taken as written, then rearranged
the final letter

explanation.surface: Canteen ladies serve stale mouldy cakes, and diners view them with distaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' looks like dinner ladies; it is the toilet. 'Ka me, ka thee' is an old proverb meaning one good turn deserves another.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to regard someone with suspicion or disapproval.

clue.text: Noodles making jazzy sound

indicators.note: jazzy means lively and improvised, so the letters are played in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone noodles on an instrument and produces a jazzy sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noodles' looks like the verb for improvising idly, which suits the jazz; it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Udon are thick Japanese wheat-flour noodles.

clue.text: Move location to contain onset of panicky breathing

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, its first letter
to contain means to hold within, so the single letter goes inside

blocks.note: to resite something is to move its location
the first letter

explanation.surface: Moving somewhere else helps to calm panicky breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing' looks like the panicky breaths; it is the noun for a pause, as in breathing space.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or relief, a breathing space.
